images.description: AlmaLinux 9 base image (RHEL-compatible). Clean install with dnf/yum package manager, bash, Python 3, curl, wget, jq, chrony, and DHCP networking pre-installed. 20GB disk. Use `dnf install -y <package>` to install software. Use `systemctl` to manage services.

Alpine Linux 3.23 base image. Minimal, security-oriented distribution with apk package manager, bash, curl, wget, chrony, and DHCP networking pre-installed. 20GB disk. Use `apk add <package>` to install software. Note: uses musl libc, not glibc.

Arch Linux rolling-release base image. Clean install with pacman package manager, systemd, bash, Python, curl, wget, jq, net-tools, chrony, and DHCP networking pre-installed. 20GB disk. Use pacman -S --noconfirm <package> to install software. Use systemctl to manage services.

CentOS Stream 10 base image (RHEL upstream). Clean install with dnf package manager, bash, Python 3, curl, wget, jq, chrony, and DHCP networking pre-installed. 20GB disk. Use `dnf install -y <package>` to install software.

CentOS 5.11 legacy base image. Clean x86_64 installation with yum, bash, Python 2.4, curl, wget, tar, OpenSSH, SysV init, DHCP networking, and antrieb user with passwordless sudo. 20GB disk. CentOS 5 is end-of-life; yum repositories point to the CentOS Vault and modern TLS/software compatibility must not be assumed.

CentOS 6.10 legacy base image. Clean x86_64 installation with yum, bash, Python 2.6, curl, wget, tar, OpenSSH, SysV init, DHCP networking, and antrieb user with passwordless sudo. 20GB disk. CentOS 6 is end-of-life; yum repositories point to the CentOS Vault and modern TLS/software compatibility must not be assumed.

Debian 13 base image. Clean Debian image with apt package manager, bash, Python 3, curl, wget, jq, net-tools, chrony, and DHCP networking pre-installed. 20GB disk. Use `apt install -y <package>` to install software. Use `systemctl` to manage services.

Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.0 base image. Clean, unregistered RHEL install with dnf, bash, Python 3, curl, wget, jq, chrony, and DHCP networking pre-installed. 20GB disk. Use systemctl to manage services. Additional package installation requires a suitable Red Hat subscription or reachable repositories.

SUBSCRIPTION CLEANUP — REQUIRED: This image ships unregistered. If you run `subscription-manager register` to reach Red Hat repositories, you MUST run `subscription-manager unregister && subscription-manager clean` as soon as the packages you need are installed. Do not defer this to the end of the session. Destroying the cluster does NOT release the entitlement — the VM is discarded, but the consumer record stays on the Red Hat portal indefinitely and has to be removed by hand. Clusters are also reaped automatically when their TTL expires, with no further tool call from you, so unregister while the node is still reachable. If you save this node as an image, unregister before calling save — otherwise every VM provisioned from your image inherits the registration.

Ubuntu Server 12.10 Quantal legacy base image (32-bit i386). Clean installation with apt, bash, Python 2.7, curl, wget, tar, OpenSSH, sudo, net-tools, DHCP networking, and antrieb user with passwordless sudo. 20GB disk. Ubuntu 12.10 is end-of-life; apt sources point to old-releases.ubuntu.com and modern TLS/software compatibility must not be assumed.

Ubuntu 16.04 LTS Xenial base image (32-bit i386 cloud image). Legacy Ubuntu environment with apt package manager, bash, Python, curl, wget, jq, net-tools, and DHCP networking. User: antrieb (passwordless sudo). Xenial is end-of-life; apt sources point at the Xenial archive and security mirrors.

Ubuntu 7.10 is end-of-life; apt sources point to old-releases.ubuntu.com and modern TLS/software compatibility must not be assumed.
